prompt: A technician is upgrading the memory in a laptop. Which memory form factor should they purchase?
explanation: Laptops use SODIMM (Small Outline DIMM) modules — physically shorter than the full-size DIMMs used in desktops.

prompt: A user's phone battery drains rapidly and the device is warm even when idle. What should the technician check FIRST?
choices: Per-app battery usage for a misbehaving app
explanation: A warm, draining phone at idle usually means an app is keeping the CPU or radios awake. Battery usage stats identify the culprit before any hardware or destructive step.

prompt: Which connector is proprietary to Apple mobile devices?
explanation: Lightning is Apple's proprietary connector, used on iPhones before the USB-C transition. Thunderbolt is an Intel/Apple port standard, not a phone connector.

prompt: A laptop display is extremely dim but barely visible when a flashlight is shined on it. What has MOST likely failed?
explanation: An image that exists but is only visible under external light means the panel is drawing but not illuminated — a failed backlight (or its inverter on older CCFL panels).

prompt: Which display technology lights each pixel individually, producing true blacks without a backlight?
explanation: OLED pixels are emissive — each one produces its own light and can turn fully off. All LCD types filter a shared backlight.

prompt: A user wants their tablet to use their phone's cellular data over a wireless connection. Which feature should they enable on the phone?
explanation: A mobile hotspot broadcasts the phone's cellular connection as a Wi-Fi network that other devices can join. Tethering over USB would require a cable.

prompt: Which port does RDP use?
explanation: Remote Desktop Protocol uses TCP 3389. Port 22 is SSH, 443 is HTTPS, 445 is SMB.

prompt: Which service translates a hostname like example.com into an IP address?
explanation: DNS resolves names to addresses. DHCP hands out IP configuration, NAT rewrites addresses at a boundary, SNMP monitors devices.

prompt: A workstation has the IP address 169.254.31.9 and cannot reach the internet. What does this address indicate?
choices: The workstation failed to contact a DHCP server
explanation: 169.254.0.0/16 is the APIPA range — a client self-assigns from it when no DHCP server responds. Check the DHCP server and the physical/link connection.

prompt: Which device forwards traffic between two different IP networks?
explanation: Routing between networks is a router's job. Switches forward frames within a LAN; APs bridge wireless clients onto that LAN; hubs just repeat signals.

prompt: Which is an advantage of the 5 GHz Wi-Fi band over 2.4 GHz?
choices: More non-overlapping channels and less interference
explanation: 5 GHz offers many more non-overlapping channels and a less crowded spectrum, at the cost of range and wall penetration — those favor 2.4 GHz.

prompt: Which DNS record type maps a hostname to an IPv4 address?
explanation: A records map names to IPv4 addresses. AAAA is IPv6, MX designates mail servers, CNAME aliases one name to another.

prompt: Which characteristic describes UDP?
choices: Establishes a connection with a three-way handshake
explanation: UDP is connectionless, best-effort transport — no handshake, no retransmission, no ordering. That low overhead suits streaming, VoIP, and DNS lookups.

prompt: Which storage option provides the LOWEST latency and highest throughput?
explanation: NVMe drives talk directly over PCIe lanes with deep command queues — Gen4 x4 reaches ~7,000 MB/s, versus ~550 MB/s for anything on the SATA III bus.

prompt: Which RAID level mirrors data across two disks with no striping?
explanation: RAID 1 writes identical data to both disks — half the capacity, survives one disk failure. RAID 0 stripes with no redundancy; 5 uses parity; 10 combines mirroring and striping.

prompt: What is the minimum number of disks required for RAID 5?
explanation: RAID 5 stripes data plus distributed parity, which requires at least three disks. It tolerates one disk failure.

prompt: What is the purpose of ECC memory?
choices: Detect and correct single-bit memory errors
explanation: ECC adds check bits that let the controller detect and fix single-bit errors in flight — essential in servers where silent corruption is unacceptable.

prompt: Which power supply connector provides main power to the motherboard?
explanation: The 24-pin ATX connector is the motherboard's main power feed. EPS (4/8-pin) powers the CPU, PCIe connectors power graphics cards, Molex is legacy peripheral power.

prompt: Into which expansion slot should a modern discrete graphics card be installed?
explanation: Graphics cards use the PCIe x16 slot for maximum lane bandwidth. x1 slots serve low-bandwidth cards; M.2 is for SSDs and wireless modules.

prompt: Which statement about DDR5 compared to DDR4 is TRUE?
choices: DDR5 modules fit in DDR4 slots
DDR5 runs at higher data rates and lower voltage
DDR5 requires more voltage than DDR4
DDR5 removed the need for memory channels
explanation: DDR5 starts around 4800 MT/s at 1.1 V (DDR4: up to ~3200 MT/s at 1.2 V) and moves power management onto the module. The keying is different — the generations are not interchangeable.

prompt: A company rents virtual machines, storage, and networking from a provider but manages the operating systems and applications itself. Which model is this?
explanation: Infrastructure as a Service supplies the raw compute/storage/network; everything from the OS up is the customer's responsibility. PaaS would also manage the OS and runtime; SaaS is the finished app.

prompt: Microsoft 365's hosted email and Office apps are an example of which cloud model?
explanation: Software as a Service — users consume a complete application; the provider runs everything beneath it.

prompt: Which hypervisor type runs directly on server hardware without a host operating system?
explanation: Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisors like ESXi, Hyper-V, and Proxmox run directly on the hardware. Type 2 hypervisors (VirtualBox, VMware Workstation) run as applications on a host OS.

prompt: Which cloud characteristic describes capacity automatically scaling up during a traffic spike and back down afterward?
explanation: Rapid elasticity is the automatic grow-and-shrink of resources with demand. Metered utilization is the pay-per-use billing that usually accompanies it.

prompt: How do containers differ from virtual machines?
choices: Containers include a full guest operating system
Containers share the host OS kernel and isolate at the process level
Containers cannot be used in production
explanation: Containers virtualize at the OS level — all containers share the host kernel, making them far lighter and faster to start than VMs, which each boot a full guest OS.

prompt: According to the CompTIA troubleshooting methodology, what is the FIRST step?
choices: Establish a theory of probable cause
explanation: Identify the problem first — gather information from the user, determine what changed, and back up before making changes. Theory, testing, plan, verification, and documentation follow.

prompt: A technician has established a theory that a bad RAM stick is causing crashes. Per the methodology, what comes NEXT?
choices: Test the theory to determine the cause
explanation: Step 3 is testing the theory (e.g., run memtest, swap sticks one at a time). Only once confirmed do you build and implement the plan of action.

prompt: A desktop shuts down under gaming load. CPU temperature reads 95°C at idle. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: Heatsink not making proper contact with the CPU
explanation: 95°C at idle points to a cooling failure — a misseated heatsink, dried thermal paste, or a dead fan. Thermal shutdowns under load are the protective response.

prompt: A drive reports a SMART error. What should the technician do FIRST?
explanation: SMART warnings mean failure is likely. Protect the data first — back it up — then plan drive replacement. Formatting or defragmenting adds stress and destroys evidence.

prompt: A PC powers on with spinning fans, but the monitor shows no signal and the board emits a repeating beep pattern. What does the beep MOST likely indicate?
choices: A hardware fault detected during POST
The monitor is in power-saving mode
explanation: Beep codes come from POST, before the OS or video initialize — commonly memory or graphics faults. Look up the pattern for that BIOS vendor and reseat the indicated component.

prompt: A laser printer produces a black vertical streak in the same position on every page. Which component is MOST likely at fault?
explanation: A repeating vertical mark is classic drum damage or debris on the drum (often integrated with the toner cartridge). Fuser problems typically smear or fail to bond toner; pickup rollers cause feed issues.

prompt: Users on 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi report intermittent drops. A scan shows nearby APs on channels 3, 6, and 9. What should the technician do?
choices: Move all APs to channel 11 together
Set APs to the non-overlapping channels 1, 6, and 11
explanation: In 2.4 GHz only channels 1, 6, and 11 don't overlap. APs on 3 and 9 bleed into neighbors and cause the interference; putting everything on one channel or raising power makes contention worse.

prompt: A workstation intermittently reboots, and inspection shows several motherboard capacitors with bulging tops. What is the appropriate fix?
explanation: Bulging or leaking capacitors are physically failing and cause instability that only worsens. Board-level component replacement isn't field-serviceable — replace the motherboard.

prompt: Place the six steps of the CompTIA troubleshooting methodology in the correct order.
items: Establish a theory of probable cause
Test the theory to determine the cause
Establish a plan of action and implement the solution
Verify full system functionality and implement preventive measures
explanation: Gather information first, hypothesize, prove the hypothesis, then plan and fix, confirm everything works (and prevent recurrence), and always document last.

prompt: Match each port number to its service.
explanation: 22 carries encrypted SSH/SFTP, 53 serves DNS lookups, 443 is TLS-encrypted web traffic, and 3389 is Remote Desktop.
